title: THE KNOWN-FAILING INPUT for the corpus-enum classifier in suites/contracts/generator-gate.ts.
$comment: NOT A CONTRACT AND NOT WALKED BY THE GENERATOR. It exists so the classifier is exercised on all three of its outcomes, because THE REAL CORPUS ONLY EVER PRODUCES TWO: every shape enum there declares a policy, so `shape + UNDECLARED` — the outcome that must make phase 2 not-due — has no instance on disk and the assertion asserting it is empty would be green whether the classifier works or never ran. `workflow.md` §11a: a check that is sound by accident is indistinguishable from one that is sound by design.

declaredShape.$comment: SHAPE + DECLARED. The ordinary case, and the mirror: if this is ever reported as undeclared the classifier is reading the wrong key.

undeclaredShape.$comment: SHAPE + UNDECLARED. *** THE ONE THE REAL CORPUS CANNOT PRODUCE. *** This is what a forgotten `enumPolicy` looks like, and it is the input the 0041 case must go red on.

gated.$comment: CONSTRAINT + UNDECLARED. Its enum is reached through `allOf/0/if/properties/kind/not` — a NEGATED CONDITIONAL, not a type. Nothing renders it, so `renderType` never counts it, so it can never carry a policy in the sense 0041 means. The real corpus has exactly one of these and it is why a pin on the RAW enum count could never reach zero.
